Troubleshooting Runtime and Environment Issues

This page collects traps actually hit in a Windows development environment: garbled Chinese output, the LLVM runtime library not being found, executables not resolving from the current directory, a missing dumpbin, and so on. After reading it, you can match a symptom quickly and fix the environment.

Garbled Chinese Output

When handling files containing Chinese in Windows PowerShell, you must explicitly use UTF-8 encoding:

# 读取
Get-Content -Encoding UTF8 path\to\file.md

# 写入（优先用编辑器/apply_patch；必须用 PowerShell 时）
Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 -Path out.md -Value $content
  • Do not use Get-Content/Set-Content/Out-File without an encoding for text files such as Chinese, Markdown, TOML, or JSON;
  • When terminal output looks garbled, re-read it as UTF-8 first to confirm, rather than concluding directly that the file contents are corrupted;
  • Prefer PowerShell 7 (C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe), which has better compatibility than Windows PowerShell 5.1.

LLVM Library Not Found / sa.exe Fails to Start

sci is built with zig build -Dllvm=true (the local LLVM is at C:\LLVM-14). When running sa.exe you need to add LLVM's library directory to PATH, otherwise the native linking stage may fail:

$env:Path = "C:\LLVM-14\lib;" + $env:Path

An exe in the Current Directory Cannot Be Executed

The local development session carries the NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 environment variable by default. It makes cmd.exe refuse to resolve batch files/executables from the current directory — even if the file is right there, it reports 'xxx' is not recognized as an internal or external command. Clear it before running a locally built CLI:

$env:NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = $null
.\zig-out\bin\sa.exe --version

Plugin Installation Tests Fail in zig build test

The plugin installation tests in zig build test depend on MSVC's dumpbin.exe, which must be added to PATH (adjust the path to your local VS version):

$env:Path = "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Community\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.44.35207\bin\Hostx64\x64;" + $env:Path

Other Environment Notes

SymptomCause and handling
zig is unavailable in a new terminalZig is provided via the user-level global PATH (such as D:\tools\zig-x86_64-windows-0.17.0\zig.exe); already-open old terminal windows need to be reopened for it to take effect.
After Set-Location in PowerShell, a child process has the wrong directoryNeither Set-Location nor [Environment]::CurrentDirectory changes pwsh's own Win32 working directory; child processes inherit the directory from when pwsh started. When you need a specific directory, use a batch script with an explicit cd /d %~dp0, or call Start-Process -WorkingDirectory.
After a batch build, the demo directory shows many changesThe demo reference product main.sa is a git-tracked file; batch builds should not write products next to the source directory; restore an accidental overwrite with git checkout -- demos.
A long test hangs the terminalWrap test/CLI execution uniformly in a timeout, for example timeout 120s ...; build commands (such as zig build --summary all) do not need it.
